"דנג'י" היה קיצור המלים "דן הג'ינג'י", כי בגלל שערו האדמוני כינוהו כך חבריו, אשר הוקירוהו והכירוהו בשל צבע-שערותיו וגובה-קומתו. היה מוכן לשחרר את כל אחד מחבריו ממשימה קשה מדי בנטלו אותה על עצמו. שש שנים ומעלה שירת ביחידתו, עבר את כל שלבי-גידולה ואף היה בין המסייעים להתפתחותה. נפל בשעת מילוי תפקידו ביום ל' בכסלו תשי"ז 4.12.1956)) והובא למנוחת-עולמים בבית-הקברות הצבאי בקרית-שאול. הניח אשה בהריונה; בתו, שנולדה שלושה-וחצי חדשים לאחר נפלו, נקראת דינה לזכרו.
cvEn:
Dan (Danji) Gonen Hiter, son of Sima and Aharon, was born on the 6th of Elul 5692 (7 September 1932) in Tel Aviv. After completing tenth grade at the Balfour Gymnasium in Tel Aviv, he transferred to the Kadoorie Agricultural School.

During the War of Independence, he filled various roles within Gadna, the youth battalions. He was drafted into the IDF's Air Force in 1950 and completed a pilot training course. He was among the small group that ferried all the Mystère aircraft from France to Israel in repeated round trips, and he also trained in France itself. He took part in the Sinai Campaign.

His comrades admired him for his diligence and self-confidence, and they felt a special affection for him because of his great friendliness. "Danji" was short for "Dan HaGinger" (Dan the Redhead), a nickname given to him by his friends, who respected and recognized him for the color of his hair and his height. He was ready to release any of his comrades from a task that was too difficult by taking it upon himself.

He served in his unit for more than six years, went through all its stages of growth, and was among those who helped develop it. He fell while performing his duty on the 30th of Kislev 5717 (4 December 1956), and was laid to rest in the military cemetery at Kiryat Shaul. He left behind a pregnant wife; their daughter, born three and a half months after his death, was named Dina in his memory.
